The signs for our classroom

On Saturday, our class ____1____ (make) small signs for the classroom. We wanted new students to find ordinary things without asking the teacher every time. The signs needed to be clear, not merely colourful.

We began with the storage ____2____ (box) beside the wall. One held pencils and another held paper. I drew a picture of each item and wrote the English word below it. The labels would stay ____3____ the classroom, where everyone could read them.

At first, ____4____ (I) idea was to use very pale yellow letters. They looked pretty on the desk, but my friend could not read them from the door. We changed to a darker colour and checked again.

Our teacher looked ____5____ (careful) at the spelling before we attached anything. She asked us to correct one missing letter, then gave us permission to put the signs in place. I decided ____6____ (wash) my hands before touching the clean paper because I had paint on my fingers.

We made another sign ____7____ the art cupboard. It was ____8____ (big) than the labels on the boxes because it needed to be seen across the room. Before ____9____ (put) it up, we checked that it would not cover the cupboard handle.

On Monday, a new pupil found the paper without help. She smiled at the drawings and asked if she could make ____10____ additional label for the reading corner. Our little project was not finished forever; another person had already found a useful next step.

Our Saturday library visit

My little brother ____1____ (visit) the library with me most Saturdays. He likes the children's room because there are low shelves and a table where he can look at pictures. I usually choose a longer story for myself.

The librarian helps several ____2____ (child) find books when we arrive. She does not choose every title for them. She asks what they enjoy and shows them where that kind of book is kept.

Last week, I borrowed ____3____ story about a family living beside the sea. It was not the book I had planned to choose. A picture on the cover caught ____4____ (I) attention, and the first page made me want to continue.

I enjoy ____5____ (read) near the window, but we cannot stay there all morning. My brother gets hungry before lunch. When he is ready, I put a marker in the book instead of trying to finish too ____6____ (quick).

We thank the librarian ____7____ her help before leaving. At home, I tell Mum why the new story seems ____8____ (interesting) than the one I read the week before. She asks about the characters rather than only the number of pages.

My brother ____9____ (choose) a comic last Saturday. He has looked through it many times and now wants to borrow another by the same writer. We put both books on the shelf beside the door so we can find them ____10____ the right time. Returning a book is part of borrowing it, even when we would like to keep reading.

It ____1____ (rain) throughout the afternoon of the school music festival. People arrived carrying umbrellas of many colours, and the staff provided a place to leave them near the entrance. The hall itself stayed dry and warm.

My friend and I put ____2____ (we) umbrellas beside each other. Mine was plain black; hers had blue flowers. We thought remembering the colours would be enough, but many other visitors had brought black umbrellas too.

At the end, we waited ____3____ the entrance was crowded. A teacher asked everyone ____4____ (go) slowly and check before taking an item. Hurrying would not make it easier to identify similar handles and covers.
